title: Error-summary labels and join both use colons, producing double-colon rows
evidence: error_summary.gleam base_label: `"guarantor_name" -> "Guarantor: name"`. application_handler.gleam:655 error tuple: `#(scope("guarantor_name"), "Your guarantor\u{2019}s full name.")`. form_pages.gleam join: `fn join_label_message(label: String, message: String) -> String { case string.ends_with(label, "?") || string.ends_with(label, "!") { True -> label <> " " <> message  False -> label <> ": " <> message } }`. Rendered row: "Guarantor: name: Your guarantor\u{2019}s full name."
detail: base_label now uses internal colons ("Guarantor: name"). join_label_message adds another ": " for non-?/! labels, so every reference/guarantor/employer/co-applicant row renders a double colon. The old em-dash join avoided this collision.
recommended_fix: In join_label_message, space-join when the label already contains a colon (like the ?/! case), or pick a non-colon sub-separator in base_label. The label-internal and label-message separators must not both be colons.
